persona.title: Pretend you are…
persona.text: Pretend you are Gary, 67. You play fantasy football in two family leagues on two different apps, and every Sunday you hop between them to see how you are doing. Your son says My Scores puts everything on one screen. Today you watch its example league to see if it would help.

challenge.intro: My Scores needs a real ESPN or Sleeper league to show your own teams, so this challenge uses its EXAMPLE league (the “Sunday Funday League”). Find each answer in the app and write it in the box under the job. When you finish, tap Check my work.
challenge.challengeNote: My Scores keeps a real league only after a real ESPN/Sleeper link, so nothing a tester does can be read from localStorage without a real account. Every job is a find-it question (check = null, selfReport) answered from the example league in the welcome tour.
challenge.start: Open My Scores. If the welcome card shows, tap '▶ Start the tour', then 'Next ›' until a card says 'Now watch it work', and tap '▶ Show me'. If the welcome card does not show, tap the ? button at the bottom right → '🎬 Take the tour again'. Keep tapping 'Next ›' slowly and read each card — the answers are on the example scoreboard behind the cards.

tasks.text: In the example league, what is the score between Your Team and Gridiron Grandpas, and who is ahead?
tasks.selfReport: Write both scores and who is ahead.
tasks.answer: Your Team 87.40, Gridiron Grandpas 74.20 — Your Team is ahead by 13.20.
tasks.hint: It is the first scoreboard card. A gold box goes around the two teams.

tasks.text: One player has a red ⏰ warning. Who is he, and what is wrong?
tasks.selfReport: Write the player and the problem.
tasks.answer: Marcus Bell (RB) is OUT, and his game starts in 45 minutes.
tasks.hint: Keep tapping Next — the red warning gets highlighted.

tasks.text: What does the 🧢 Assistant Manager suggest you do about it?
tasks.answer: Bench Marcus Bell and play Jay Monroe instead (Lineup suggestions).
tasks.hint: The Assistant Manager box opens a few cards later. Look under LINEUP SUGGESTIONS.

tasks.text: Who is first in the league standings, and what is their record?
tasks.selfReport: Write the team and its wins-losses.
tasks.hint: Near the end of the tour the STANDINGS show.

tasks.text: After the tour, try to add a team with this made-up link: yahoo.com/myteam. Which two fantasy apps does My Scores work with?
tasks.answer: ESPN and Sleeper (a Yahoo link gets a friendly 'doesn't look like an ESPN or Sleeper link').
tasks.hint: Tap 'Let’s go ›' at the end of the tour, paste the link, tap 'Find my league' and read the message.

ownWords.question: In your own words, what is this app for?
keyIdeas: puts all your fantasy football teams from different leagues on one screen
works with ESPN and Sleeper leagues, one button to update
warns about players who are out and suggests lineup changes

lines: This video explains My Scores from the very beginning. If you have never seen it, that is fine.
First, the everyday problem. Lots of families play fantasy football, often in more than one league, on more than one app. On a Sunday that means hopping between apps to see how everyone is doing.
My Scores puts every team you follow on one screen, yours and your opponent's, with one button to update them all. It works with ESPN and Sleeper leagues.
It is for anyone who plays, from one team to a whole family's worth. And if you run a league, it has tools for that too.
What you see here is an example league, so you can see how it looks before you add your own.
There are four screens: Add a team, My teams, your Scores, and real NFL scores. First, adding a team. It asks one question at a time: where do you play this team?
Open your team in the ESPN or Sleeper app or website, copy the page's link, and paste it in this box. Then tap Find my league.
Yahoo, CBS and NFL dot com don't allow this yet. This box says so.
Next it lists every team in the league. Tap yours. Then tap plus Add another team if you play in another league, or I'm done to see your scores.
My teams lists every team the app follows. First puts a team at the top, and Remove stops following one, after asking.
Now the Scores screen. Each team gets a card: the league, ESPN or Sleeper, and whether the game is live, final or not started.
Your team on the left, your opponent on the right: score, projection and record. The chips count players playing now, finished, or still waiting.
Underneath: whether you're ahead or behind, by how much, and your odds of winning.
A red warning means one of your starters is out and his game starts soon. Time to swap him.
Tap either side to open that team's roster, bench underneath. Green is playing now, yellow not started, grey finished, purple a bye.
A hurt player has a tag: O for out, Q for questionable. Tap his row to read the latest injury news.
Show Assistant Manager spots trouble for you. Lineup suggestions find a bench player projected to beat a starter.
Check available players finds the best free agents for a hurt or bye-week starter, and bye weeks shows who is off this week and next.
Or type something plain in the Ask box, like replace my quarterback.
For ESPN teams, kickoff alerts message your phone when a starter is out and his game is about to start.
Swipe the card sideways for the other games in your league...
...then the standings and the latest pickups and trades. It loops back to your game.
Update scores sits at the bottom of the screen. Tap it any time for the newest numbers.
Below your cards: See real NFL scores shows every real game this week, and League manager tools tracks dues, contacts, group messages and a weekly recap.
Your first two minutes: open your team on ESPN or Sleeper, copy the link, paste it here, tap Find my league, and tap your team. Done.
Privacy: no account and no sign-up. Your teams are kept on this phone, and scores come straight from ESPN or Sleeper. Kickoff alerts, if you turn them on, go through a small Daraja relay.
My Scores is free.
And the question mark button in the corner has the tour, bigger text and help, any time.

daily.task: In My Scores, change one thing: a pick, a dues payment or a made-up contact in the league manager tools.
